country.comment: Studied communities in subnormal agglomerations (irregular/favela settlements) in the Baixada Santista metropolitan region, São Paulo state, Brazil.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Affiliations & Abstract; PDF p. 2, Introdução; PDF p. 3, Metodologia e objetivo

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive survey percentages and chart bars (Gráfico 1) only; no inferential statistical models, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported. Note an internal discrepancy in the text regarding CADUNICO enrollment (<25% reported on PDF p. 5 col. 1 vs. 57% reported on PDF p. 5 col. 2).
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive percentages only (N = 68 community leaders representing ~6,800 of 14,079 households in irregular settlements of Baixada Santista, SP; no regression estimates, CIs, or p-values reported): under the utility's 'inclusive universalization' model (monthly multi-stakeholder community meetings and 24/7 utility community agents), the majority of interviewed leaders in irregular/risk areas had formal utility water supply, water tanks, and did not rely on water trucks; however, 25% still lived near open sewage, lacked a household sewer connection, and were in flood zones due to remaining technical, economic, or legal impediments. Low household enrollment in the social water tariff was observed (Gráfico 1, items 37-38), attributed to user lack of knowledge of registration procedures, eligibility rules detached from informal livelihoods (only 35% in the formal economy; leaders lacked proof of income), and low social-registry coverage (<25% reported for Bolsa Família/CADUNICO in Results, though Discussion reports 57% in CADUNICO). Additionally, 50% reported widespread water-bill non-payment and community leaks, while 100% reported leaks to the utility's community agent.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 4, Resultados & Gráfico 1; PDF p. 5, Resultados & Discussão

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the non-experimental cross-sectional survey/case-study design. Assigned 2 because the study directly documents and observes the institutional/administrative mechanisms operating on service access: (a) the utility's community-agent interface (24/7 social workers/sociologists) and monthly participatory meetings enabling formal water provision in irregular settlements, (b) remaining legal/tenure impediments blocking sewerage connections for 25% of respondents, and (c) procedural ignorance and informal-income documentation barriers limiting social tariff enrollment.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 3, Introdução & Metodologia e objetivo; PDF p. 4, Gráfico 1; PDF p. 5, Resultados & Discussão

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines land tenure/irregularity and lack of proof of income (ELIGIBILITY: tenure, documentation), social tariff affordability/entry costs and lack of knowledge of registration procedures (BURDEN: fees, procedural_steps), and 'inclusive universalization' socio-technical arrangements in irregular areas via monthly deliberative meetings, 24/7 utility community agents, debt negotiation, and multi-agency coordination across utility, municipality, CONSEG, ministries, and Public Prosecutor's Office (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: accommodation, participation, bureaucratic_assistance, political_coordination).
